description_full: BW LPG Limited, an investment holding company, engages in ship owning and chartering activities worldwide. It operates through Shipping and Product Services segments. The company engages in the transportation of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG); provision of integrated LPG delivery services, as well as management services; wholesale and trade of LPG; and investment in commercial enterprises. As of December 31, 2025, it owned and operated a fleet of 54 vessels, including 28 very large gas carriers, 7 large gas carriers time chartered in by product services, and 8 VLGCs owned by BW LPG India Pte. Ltd. BW LPG Limited was formerly known as BW Gas LPG Holding Limited and changed its name to BW LPG Limited in September 2013. The company was founded in 1935 and is headquartered in Singapore.

financial_summary: BW LPG Limited is a mid-cap energy business with a $3.3B market cap.
Returns on capital run at 16% against a 9% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.
The business throws off $385M in free cash flow, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.96× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.8% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 6.6×.

Management returns a meaningful 7.3% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 36% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

growth: At current returns, reinvesting 25% of profits supports about 4.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
